title: Cost optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Sanjay Patel
release_notes: Automated autotuning for batching/caching defaults; quantization profile registry & selection heuristics; unit-economics (UEcon) CLI and Console integration for per-route cost recommendations
description:
Motivation: Customers running large volumes of inference need lower unit costs without manual tuning. This PR implements an end-to-end automation for cost optimizations: autotuned batching and KV-prefix caching defaults, a small quantization profile registry with automatic selection heuristics, and the first pass of the unit-economics toolkit (CLI + console integration) to expose recommended settings per-route.

What this change does: consolidated changes across runtime, control plane, and observability: 1) Runtime: added an autotuner that observes latency percentiles, effective batching sizes, and cache hit rates to suggest and optionally apply batching window and cache TTL defaults per route. 2) Quant profiles: introduces a lightweight registry (config-driven) of quantization profiles (fp16/int8/4-bit candidates) and runtime selection logic that matches profile eligibility to model architecture, sequence length, and target latency headroom. 3) Unit-econ tooling: a CLI (tools/uecon) to compute per-token cost estimates from telemetry and to generate recommended config patches; Console dashboard wiring to display recommendations and projected savings.

Compatibility and rollout: defaults are opt-in behind a feature flag (cost_autotune_v1) and we ship a suggestion-only mode by default. A staged rollout plan is included: telemetry collection -> suggest mode -> opt-in auto-apply for non-critical routes -> canary auto-apply -> wider rollout. All changes are reversible via feature flags and route config overrides.

Tests & results: microbenchmarks run on prod-like clusters show median token cost reduction of 18% (best-effort routes) and p95 latency impact < 3% for tuned routes. Unit and integration tests added for tuner logic, quant selection, and CLI output formatting.

Operational notes: added tracing spans and Prometheus metrics (batch_autotune_iterations_total, batch_autotune_applied_total, quant_profile_selected_total, uecon_recommendations_generated_total). Alerts: created an alert for tuning-induced latency regressions (tuning_latency_regression_high).

Files of interest: see changed_files list.

Follow-ups: ENG-3410 (auto-apply policy UI), ENG-3425 (refine quant quality-aware evaluation), PM-720 (cost-savings dashboard in Console).
commits: Initial implementation: runtime autotuner and basic heuristics
Add quantization profile registry and selection logic
Unit-econ CLI + recommendation engine + Console wiring
review_comments: Elena Ruiz: The autotuner looks promising. Two asks: (1) add a safety window for p95 regressions before applying changes; (2) ensure cache TTL changes don't invalidate persisted KV entries unexpectedly.

Author (Sanjay): Added p95 safety guard and a conservative dry-run period by default. Cache TTL change path now emits a migration-safe event and preserves old keys for 24h. See autotuner.go:applyWithSafety and cache_autotune.go:migrateIfNeeded.
Marco Li: Can we see the metrics cardinality impact? The new per-route metrics might explode.
Author: Aggregated the metrics by route-group and added sampling; updated metrics_registry.yaml accordingly.
ci_summary: integration-tests: flaky (one timeout on first run), rerun passed
notes: Backported small fix to release/2024-11 for urgent customer pilot (hotfix branch created). Suggest monitoring uecon_recommendations_generated_total and tuning_latency_regression_high for first 72h post-merge.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: autotuning can temporarily increase latency while probing. Mitigations: default suggest-only mode, p95 safety checks, conservative initial thresholds, canary-only auto-apply for first 10% of routes.
notes_for_changelog: Introduce cost autotuning (experimental): suggests batching/caching and quantization settings; includes UEcon tooling to estimate per-route savings. Feature gated and opt-in by default.
